gen-dafont-disorder-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight keeps its ascenders short and its curve tails pulled back. Disorder is the raw, chaotic one, with big lowercase and glyphs spaced far apart, while the sans-serif body stays modern and tidy.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-karla: Raw letters, spaced wide, with no swelling at the joins. Disorder does chaos best, thin-looking strokes that never actually thin, while Karla does approachable best with a stocky, open-mouthed build.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-khula: Raw is the right word for Disorder, with its big lowercase and glyphs spaced well apart. And Khula, modern and sans-serif, softens it with a deep midsection and curves that keep their mouths open.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-krub: Disorder draws its round letters with walls as hefty as the straight ones, and its glyphs sit well apart. Krub, a sans with a pronounced x-height, takes over where Disorder gets loud.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-michroma: Wide-spaced and contemporary, the sans body gives every letter a generous margin on both sides. Michroma feels measured beside Disorder, whose raw, chaotic strokes never vary in thickness at all.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Disorder goes for raw chaos, its glyphs set far apart and its lowercase big. Mochiy Pop P One does clean and approachable, with wide spacing and no pointed-brush swell.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-mozilla-headline: Raw letters, joins as sturdy as the stems, glyphs spaced wide. The best part is Disorder's raw chaos set against Mozilla Headline's approachable, big-bodied lowercase and a splayed c terminal.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-mozilla-text: Mozilla Text reads sturdy, its terminals flaring outward. Next to Disorder's raw, chaotic curves, which match their stems exactly, it brings a steadier, more measured voice to the layout.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans: Disorder brings raw chaos, with big lowercase and tails and terminals as sturdy as the main stems. But Noto Sans, with its wide-open c, is the plain-spoken foil that makes that chaos land.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-anatoli: Disorder never varies its stroke weight, and its glyphs sit far apart. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs steadies that raw chaos with outward-pointing terminals and lowercase rising close to cap height.
